relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a girl with a TNFAIP3 variant: "The analysis identified a likely pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3".
method_note: Read the whole paper and built the JSON by hand-entered values in a small Python script (no table transcribed by script); all spans checked verbatim by script. One unnamed patient, labelled 'patient'. Table 1 (laboratory investigations) has two parameter/result column pairs; only CRP (weakly positive), ANA (negative) and celiac serology (negative) were used as features; Hb 10.6 g/dL and other values were not interpreted because the paper does not call them abnormal. Variants: PIK3R1, HBB, SERPINA1 (described as 'Additional variants', count per gene not stated; one row per gene) and a VUS in VPS37A are attributed to this patient but no variant description is printed, so variant_original_string is 'not reported'. variant_type 'frameshift' rests on the printed 'fs' notation only; zygosity not stated for this patient (only generically for HA20; parents consanguineous), so 'not reported'. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) TNFAIP3 pathogenicity is 'likely pathogenic' (abstract, case), 'pathogenic' (introduction) and 'probable pathogenic' (discussion). (2) The other-gene variants are 'possibly modifying the phenotype'/'potential modifier role' but the discussion says 'They do not modify or explain the core HA20 phenotype'. (3) Onset: abstract 'from age 2' vs case text 'from the age of second year' (could mean age 1-2); title says 'Infantile Onset'; the only event in infancy is a febrile seizure the authors call possibly comorbid or coincidental. Recorded 'from age 2'. (4) Eye redness, pain and eyelid swelling during flares, yet 'ophthalmologic ... investigation ... were negative'; uveitis/ocular inflammation checklist left 'not reported'. (5) Abdominal pain, diarrhea and perianal swelling 'resembling hemorrhoidal inflammation', yet GI investigation negative and no IBD findings; GI ulcers/inflammation checklist left 'not reported'. Checklist judgments: CNS involvement marked observed from the infantile febrile convulsive seizure; elevated inflammatory markers observed from 'CRP | Weakly Positive' (timing relative to flares not stated; ESR 14 mm/hr not called abnormal); autoantibodies left 'not reported' because only ANA and celiac serology were negative (narrow absence vs composite item). Age at last evaluation recorded as '5-year-old' (age as described in the report; follow-up continued eight months after infliximab). Vital status not stated. Sanger confirmation of the WES variants in patient and parents was planned but not done.
